Paragraph: Rama, on arriving at that Lake of Lotuses called Pampa along with Lakshmana, which is full with lotuses, costuses, and fishes, lamented as his emotions are disturbed, on seeing the beauty of the Lake comparable with Seetha's face.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arriving at Lake Pampa, Rama experiences heightened emotional distress and grief upon seeing the beautiful surroundings, which remind him of his abducted wife, Seetha.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama gives expression to his deep sorrow and inner disturbance, allowing his longing and grief for Seetha to manifest in the presence of his loyal brother, Lakshmana.
Outcome/Resolution: Rama openly laments, marking the beginning of his intense struggle with longing and sorrow while exploring the wilderness of Kishkindha.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Emotional Regulation: Emotional Overflow, Expressive Coping, Coping Difficulty

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Viraha DuHkha (Pain of Separation/Grief from loss of beloved)
Akulendriya (Disturbed senses/emotions under intense mental distress)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The passage reflects the human manifestation of the Divine experiencing Viraha (separation). Rama sees the natural beauty as a reflection of Seetha and creation, acknowledging the agony of souls separated from the Divine.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse illustrates the onset of acute grief triggering sensory and emotional agitation (Akulendriya). Environmental triggers (the beauty of the lake) serve as psychological reminders of loss, initiating intense emotional grief.
